headline: Nature stories at mac today + Bournville open day Saturday
summary: Outdoor Stories 4 Nature at mac this morning; free Aldridge/Solihull rhymes today; Friday library play; Saturday stacks Bournville Heritage Open Day, Walsall hippo workshops, Honey Show and campus storytelling.

notices.title: Weather (Met Office Birmingham)
notices.detail: Thu 10 fine/sunny morning ~19°C then cloud and rain/breezier from late afternoon/evening (rain chance rising ~40–60% from 6–8pm). Fri 11 brighter with sunny intervals ~21°C after any early damp. Sat 12 cloudy ~22°C, rain chance ~30% from midday with gusts up to ~32mph — outdoor Heritage plans fine with a layer; pack a rain shell. Sun 13 improving to sunny intervals ~21°C after early damp.

datedPicks.title: Stories 4 Nature at mac Birmingham
datedPicks.location: mac Birmingham (Outdoor Terrace), Cannon Hill Park, Birmingham B12 9QH
datedPicks.cost: Pay what you choose (adults free, no adult ticket needed)
datedPicks.description: Outdoor nature storytelling and messy sensory crafts for ages 1–5 with grown-ups — led by Juliet (storyteller / forest school). Dress for the weather; outdoor terrace.
datedPicks.bookingStatus: book child tickets — pay what you choose
datedPicks.parentHeadsUp: Adults go free and do not book. Outdoor morning — Met Office fine until afternoon rain/breeze. Book Thu 10 Sep 10.30 instance.
datedPicks.whyPicked: NEW same-day outdoor nature story/craft at Cannon Hill — distinctive vs library rhymes; organiser-dated Thu 10.

datedPicks.title: Bournville Heritage Open Day
datedPicks.location: Bournville village (19 free sites; hub around Village Green / Selly Manor), Bournville, Birmingham B30
datedPicks.cost: Free (most sites drop-in; Almshouses / Cadbury Archives / Cadbury World pre-book tours sold out)
datedPicks.description: Heritage Open Days / Birmingham Heritage Week: 19 historic Bournville sites open free with tours, exhibitions, vintage vehicles, model boats, family fun and a Manor Farm Park heritage trail (tours 11am & 2pm). Map + programme on BVT page.
datedPicks.bookingStatus: free drop-in (limited sold-out pre-book tours only)
datedPicks.parentHeadsUp: Limited parking — prefer public transport. Cadbury World/Almshouses/Archives free tour tickets sold out; everything else open without booking. Download BVT map/programme.
datedPicks.whyPicked: Re-verified free Sat garden-village open day across 19 sites — strongest weekend family heritage product.
datedPicks.street: Bournville Village Green / 350 Bournville Lane area

datedPicks.title: Walsall Hippo Trail exhibition & art workshops
datedPicks.location: The New Art Gallery Walsall, Gallery Square, Walsall WS2 8LG
datedPicks.description: Free drop-in family day: youth hippo artworks on show plus hands-on workshops (drawing, clay, zines, leather craft) feeding the 2027 Walsall Hippo sculpture trail. With Urban Hax and RicNic.
datedPicks.sourceName: Walsall Council / New Art Gallery Walsall
datedPicks.parentHeadsUp: Free family-friendly; all ages welcome. Strong indoor Sat option if breezy/showery.
datedPicks.whyPicked: Re-verified free Sat kids art day in Walsall — distinctive local craft, not a tourist pad.

datedPicks.title: Birmingham Honey Show at Winterbourne

datedPicks.cost: Free (Heritage Open Days — check in at reception)
datedPicks.description: Free weekend honey celebration with Birmingham Beekeepers: live hive demos, local honey stalls, family activities, plus free entry to the house and gardens as part of Heritage Open Days.

datedPicks.parentHeadsUp: Sat hive demos 11.30, 13.30, 15.30. Limited free on-site parking. Part of Heritage Open Days / Heritage Week.
datedPicks.whyPicked: Re-verified free Sat–Sun family nature day at Winterbourne — strong Edgbaston weekend option.

datedPicks.title: Heritage for All at The Exchange (+ Barber family workshop)
datedPicks.location: The Exchange, 3 Centenary Square, Birmingham B1 2DR
datedPicks.description: Free Birmingham Heritage Week drop-in: vaults exhibition, building tours, family heritage trail, and Barber Institute “Reimagine the Archive” family art workshop (ideal ages 4–10). Café open.
datedPicks.parentHeadsUp: Part of Birmingham Heritage Week (11–20 Sep). No booking. Step-free + Changing Places toilet.
datedPicks.whyPicked: Re-verified free Sat city-centre heritage day with kids art workshop.

datedPicks.title: Storytelling & Sculpture: beneath your feet!
datedPicks.location: Meet outside Sport & Fitness Centre, University of Birmingham, Edgbaston B15 2TT
datedPicks.description: 30-minute family storytelling with Cat Weatherill at the Mining Department Heraldic Shield, then free sculpture-park wander. Max 20 per slot; arrive 5 minutes early.
datedPicks.bookingStatus: free — capacity 20/slot; arrive early to check in
datedPicks.parentHeadsUp: Recommended ages 5+. Primarily outdoors — water, caps. Level access with some uneven ground. Goes ahead in light rain.
datedPicks.whyPicked: Re-verified free Sat campus storytelling for 5+ — short distinctive Heritage Week family slot.

datedPicks.title: Morning Explorers at Thinktank (autism-friendly)
datedPicks.cost: Admission charges apply (Members free entry but must pre-book; optional planetarium extra)
datedPicks.description: Second-Saturday autism-friendly morning: early entry from 9am, quieter galleries (sounds muted to 11am), ear defenders/sensory maps. MiniBrum/science garden from 9.30am.
datedPicks.parentHeadsUp: Tourist-staple venue — labelled accessibility backup only. Paid admission; book ahead. Sat 12 Sep confirmed.
datedPicks.whyPicked: Re-verified Sat 12 Morning Explorers — distinctive accessibility slot, not a generic Thinktank pad.
